question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Goa Inquisition locations and historical associations]
options: Old Goa — Headquarters of the Goa Inquisition housed in the Palace of the Inquisition (Casa da Inquisição)
Panaji — Port city where the first Auto-da-fé public sentencing ceremony was held in 1563
Cochin — Southern enclave where local Syrian Christians and Jews came under the scrutiny of the Inquisition's agents
Cuncolim — South Goa village where resistance to forced conversions culminated in the killing of Jesuit priests in 1583
wrong_fact: The Auto-da-fé ceremonies were held in Old Goa (specifically in front of the Sé Cathedral), not Panaji, which became the administrative capital much later (1843).
explanation: Auto-da-fé ceremonies (acts of faith involving public penance and sentencing) were held in the square outside the Sé Cathedral in Old Goa, the capital at the time. Panaji did not serve as the capital or the center of the Inquisition during the 16th century. Cochin, Old Goa, and Cuncolim are accurately associated with their respective events.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Territorial reach and enforcement of the Goa Inquisition]
options: Palace of the Sabaio — The grand structure in Old Goa belonging to Adil Shah that was repurposed into the Inquisition Palace
Bardez and Salcete — Surrounding provinces of Goa where Inquisition laws strictly banned public Hindu rites and destroyed local shrines
Diu and Daman — Northern enclaves where commissioners (comissários) of the Inquisition were sent to enforce Holy Office edicts
Bombay — Port town where the Portuguese Inquisition established its second permanent tribunal in 1610 to trial crypto-Jews
wrong_fact: The Portuguese Inquisition in Asia had only one tribunal, which was located in Goa. No secondary tribunal was ever established in Bombay.
explanation: The Goa Inquisition had a single central tribunal in Goa. It monitored other territories like Daman, Diu, Cochin, and East Africa through visiting commissioners, but never set up a second tribunal, let alone in Bombay (which was ceded to the British in 1661). The Palace of the Sabaio served as the headquarters, and Bardez/Salcete saw intense enforcement.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Historical geography and jurisdiction of the Inquisition]
options: Archbishopric of Goa — The primary ecclesiastical see whose Archbishop exercised overall spiritual patronage (Padroado) during the Inquisition
Udayamperoor (Diamper) — Venue of the 1599 Synod that paved the way for the Inquisition's authority over Syrian Christian practices
Rua Direita (Old Goa) — Central street location of the Aljube, the ecclesiastical prison where Inquisition suspects were detained
Chaul — Fortified port town where the central Inquisition tribunal was temporarily moved during the Maratha invasion of Goa in 1683
wrong_fact: The Inquisition tribunal was never relocated from Old Goa during the Maratha invasion of 1683. It remained in the capital throughout its history.
explanation: The Inquisition tribunal remained permanently at the Casa da Inquisição in Old Goa until its final abolition in 1812 (with a brief temporary suspension in 1774–1778). It was never relocated to Chaul. The Archbishopric of Goa, the Synod of Diamper (Udayamperoor), and the Aljube prison on Rua Direita are historically correct.
